articles.title: India's Economy Grows 7.8% in April-June, Beating All Forecasts
articles.excerpt: GDP growth in Q1 FY2027 comfortably surpassed the 7.1% consensus and the RBI's 7% projection, driven by a surge in manufacturing and investment activity.
articles.nri_angle: India's strong growth run — potentially the fourth consecutive year above 7% — could support equity markets and attract portfolio inflows, with implications for NRI investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata Motors EV Bookings Triple as Company Bets on Record Festive Quarter
articles.excerpt: India's largest EV maker has seen a three-fold surge in electric vehicle bookings over six months but faces supply constraints as it targets the industry's biggest-ever September-December quarter.
articles.image_caption: Tata Nexon EV, India's best-selling electric vehicle. The company reported a threefold jump in EV bookings ahead of the festive quarter.
articles.nri_angle: Tata Motors' EV push reflects India's rapid shift toward electric mobility, a transformation closely watched by diaspora investors and NRIs considering vehicle purchases during visits home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Passes Bill to Reintroduce Fees on UPI Merchant Payments
articles.excerpt: After six years of zero charges that fueled the world's largest real-time payment system, New Delhi will allow banks to levy merchant fees on large UPI transactions while keeping person-to-person payments free.
articles.image_caption: India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI). The government passed a bill amending the Payment and Settlement Systems Act to allow merchant fees on UPI and RuPay debit card transactions.
articles.nri_angle: UPI operates in 11 countries and increasingly serves as a remittance channel for the Indian diaspora, making the fee structure directly relevant to NRI payments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stock Futures Slide as U.S. Strikes on Iran Rattle Global Markets
articles.excerpt: Oil prices surge past $90 a barrel and Asian equities tumble after U.S. forces hit Iranian launchers on Larak Island, reigniting fears of a wider Middle East escalation.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, where U.S. forces struck Iranian launchers on Larak Island. The military escalation sent global stock futures sliding and crude oil prices surging.
articles.nri_angle: Rising oil prices and potential Fed rate hikes could increase inflationary pressure on U.S. households, including the Indian diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Meets Fiscal Deficit Target for FY26 as Credit Ratings Improve, Sitharaman Says
articles.excerpt: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman told the Indian diaspora in Chicago that India achieved its fiscal deficit goal of 4.4% of GDP for 2025-26 and is targeting a debt-to-GDP ratio of 50% by 2030.
articles.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman addresses the Indian diaspora in Chicago during her nine-day official visit to Canada and the United States. She confirmed India met its fiscal deficit target of 4.4% of GDP for FY26.
articles.nri_angle: Finance Minister Sitharaman delivered the fiscal update while addressing the Indian diaspora community in Chicago during a nine-day US-Canada visit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Economy on Track for 7% Growth in FY27 Despite Global Headwinds, EY Says
articles.excerpt: A recent EY report projects India's real GDP growth at 7-7.2% in FY27, supported by robust industrial output, a government capex rebound, and strong credit growth, even as inflation and weaker trade conditions pose risks.
articles.image_caption: India's economy is on track for 7% real GDP growth in FY27, according to EY, driven by industrial expansion, rising private investment, and strong domestic consumption.
articles.nri_angle: India's projected 7% growth in FY27 reinforces the investment case for NRIs and diaspora businesses with exposure to the Indian market.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HDFC Bank Weighs Deputy MD Bharucha and External Candidate for CEO Succession
articles.excerpt: India's largest private lender is fast-tracking its leadership search after CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan announced he will not seek reappointment when his term ends in October.
articles.image_caption: HDFC Bank, India's largest private-sector lender. The bank is weighing Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha and an external candidate for CEO succession.
articles.nri_angle: HDFC Bank's leadership transition matters directly to NRI investors and depositors who hold significant stakes in India's largest private lender.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ex-MP Somaiya Seeks Probe Into Sensex's Wild 2,200-Point Swing
articles.excerpt: Former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya demands SEBI suspend its new Closing Auction Session mechanism after a five-minute crash and recovery on August 27.
articles.image_caption: Former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya. He has written to SEBI demanding a temporary suspension of the Closing Auction Session mechanism after the Sensex crashed over 2,200 points on August 27.
articles.nri_angle: Relevant for Indian diaspora investors with exposure to Indian equities through direct holdings or mutual funds. Market structure changes at NSE/BSE directly affect portfolio valuations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan to Step Down After Three Decades
articles.excerpt: India's largest private lender fast-tracks succession search as Jagdishan declines reappointment, ending a turbulent chapter marked by boardroom friction and a 27% share price decline.
articles.image_caption: HDFC Bank, India's largest private-sector lender. CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan is stepping down after three decades with the bank, marking a major leadership transition.
articles.nri_angle: HDFC Bank is one of the most widely used banks for NRI accounts, remittances, and cross-border services. Leadership instability and the 27% share decline directly affect diaspora banking and investment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Sugar Prices Hit Record Highs as Government Races to Cool Market Before Diwali
articles.excerpt: New Delhi tightens stock limits and opens duty-free imports for the first time in nearly a decade as festival season demand meets a crop shortfall.
articles.image_caption: Sugarcane fields in India. Sugar prices have hit record highs as the government races to cool the market before Diwali.
articles.nri_angle: Record sugar prices ahead of Diwali affect the cost of traditional sweets and festival preparations for NRI families with connections to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Marvell Technology Shares Tumble 8% Despite Earnings Beat on Google Deal Uncertainty
articles.excerpt: The chipmaker posted record data center revenue and raised its fiscal-year forecast, but investors punished the stock after management offered vague timelines on a blockbuster Google partnership.
articles.image_caption: Marvell Technology headquarters. The chipmaker's shares fell 8% despite beating Q2 revenue estimates, amid uncertainty over a key Google deal.
articles.nri_angle: Marvell has significant engineering operations in India and its custom chip partnerships shape the AI infrastructure ecosystem where Indian-origin engineers are heavily represented.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canadian Economy Surges 3.3 Percent in Q2, Fastest Growth Since 2023
articles.excerpt: Strong export recovery and solid consumer spending propelled Canada's economic rebound, but a new round of US tariffs casts a shadow over the outlook.
articles.nri_angle: Canada's economic recovery matters to the large Indian diaspora in Canada, particularly those in manufacturing and technology sectors affected by trade uncertainty.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fed Chair Warsh Signals Rate Hikes Possible as Inflation Stays Elevated
articles.excerpt: In his debut Jackson Hole speech, Kevin Warsh said the Fed will 'have work to do' if inflation does not return to target, sending markets to price in 55 percent odds of a September rate hike.
articles.nri_angle: Fed rate decisions directly impact mortgage rates, borrowing costs, and investment returns for millions of Indian Americans, while rate hikes could strengthen the dollar against the rupee.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Faces Recession Risk as Trade War With US Threatens 100,000 Jobs
articles.excerpt: Economists warn that a collapse of the USMCA free trade agreement could push Canada onto a 'permanently lower path,' with the auto sector bracing for 50 percent tariffs starting in 2027.
articles.nri_angle: The US-Canada trade war directly impacts the large Indian diaspora in Canada, particularly in manufacturing-heavy provinces like Ontario where many South Asian communities are concentrated.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sensex Snaps Two-Day Losing Streak on IT Surge but Posts Third Straight Weekly Loss
articles.excerpt: IT stocks rally 3.5% on Nvidia earnings boost while new closing auction mechanism and Fed speech jitters weigh on weekly performance
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. The Sensex snapped a two-day losing streak on an IT sector surge but posted its third straight weekly loss.
articles.nri_angle: Indian stock market performance directly affects NRI portfolios and mutual fund investments, with the IT sector rally particularly relevant given the large Indian tech diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jio Platforms Gets SEBI Green Light for $3.8 Billion IPO, India's Biggest
articles.excerpt: India's markets regulator cleared the Reliance subsidiary's offering on Friday, setting the stage for a listing that would surpass Hyundai Motor India's 2024 record.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries. Jio Platforms, a subsidiary of Reliance, has received SEBI approval for what would be India's largest-ever IPO at $3.8 billion.
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors face access barriers to India's domestic IPO market, making direct participation in the Jio listing difficult without Indian demat accounts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Forex Reserves Hit Record $729 Billion on NRI Deposit Surge
articles.excerpt: The RBI's concessional swap facility drew nearly $73 billion in overseas inflows since June, pushing reserves past their February peak and prompting an early closure of the deposit window.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee banknotes. India's foreign exchange reserves reached a record $729.33 billion in the week ended August 21, driven by a surge in overseas deposit inflows under the RBI's concessional swap facility.
articles.image_credit: Photo by Mayur Freelancer on Pexels
articles.nri_angle: Record reserves and a stronger RBI balance sheet support rupee stability and improve the macro backdrop for NRI investments and remittances.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: RBI Dollar-Rupee Swap Draws $72.85 Billion as NRI Deposit Window Closes Monday
articles.excerpt: The FCNR-B deposit scheme, which raised $65.4 billion in 75 days, has been closed early due to overwhelming demand. NRIs have until August 31 to lock in 6-7.5% returns on dollar deposits.
articles.nri_angle: The FCNR-B scheme directly impacts NRI depositors who can lock in 6-7.5% returns on dollar-denominated deposits with Indian banks, with the window closing August 31.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Offer NRIs Up to 19x Leverage on FCNR Deposits as RBI Deadline Nears
articles.excerpt: Banks have mobilized $65 billion in FCNR deposits in 75 days as RBI's concessional swap facility deadline approaches August 31, with leveraged structures promising equity-like dollar returns.
articles.nri_angle: Directly relevant to NRIs considering parking dollar savings in India for guaranteed returns before the RBI window closes on August 31.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Gold and Silver ETFs Fall Up to 2.3% as Import Duty Cut Speculation Grips Market
articles.excerpt: Gold and silver exchange-traded funds in India tumbled Thursday even as global prices held steady, as investors priced in a possible rollback of import duties from 15% to 6%.
articles.image_caption: Gold bullion bars. Indian gold and silver ETFs fell up to 2.3 percent amid speculation that the government may cut import duties on precious metals.
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors holding Indian gold and silver ETFs face potential repricing from duty changes, while the policy shift could affect gold prices for diaspora families purchasing jewellery in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRI Deposits Drop 23% as Diaspora Savers Shift to Dollar Accounts
articles.excerpt: Fresh deposit inflows from non-resident Indians fell to $2.78 billion in the April-June quarter, with a 93% plunge in rupee accounts offset by a doubling of foreign-currency deposits following RBI intervention.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai. NRI deposits fell 23 percent as diaspora savers shifted toward dollar-denominated FCNR accounts.
articles.nri_angle: Directly affects NRIs managing savings and remittances to India, with a clear shift from rupee to dollar-denominated accounts reflecting currency risk concerns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HDFC Bank AT1 Bond Nightmare Deepens as West Asia NRIs Renew Complaints Over $100 Million Losses
articles.excerpt: About 70 NRI investors in the UAE and Bahrain have resurfaced grievances over Credit Suisse bonds sold between 2017 and 2019 that were later written down to zero.
articles.image_caption: An HDFC Bank branch in India. NRI investors in West Asia have renewed complaints over approximately 100 million dollars in losses from the bank's AT1 bond writedown.
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors in the UAE and Bahrain are directly affected, raising concerns about protections for diaspora members who maintain financial ties with India through overseas banking products.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hormuz Crisis Costs Fossil Fuel Importers $330 Billion as India Pays $22 Billion Extra
articles.excerpt: A new CREA analysis finds the six-month energy price shock is the largest since the 1990 Gulf War, with low-income countries bearing a disproportionate burden.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil transit chokepoint. The ongoing crisis has cost fossil fuel importers $330 billion, with India paying an extra $22 billion.
articles.nri_angle: India has paid $22 billion extra for fossil fuel imports since the crisis began, threatening household energy costs and inflation for families both in India and across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HDFC Bank Faces US Class Action Over Alleged Deposit Scheme and Securities Fraud
articles.excerpt: India's largest private lender has been sued in a New York federal court by investors alleging that the bank disguised payments as marketing expenses to induce deposits from a Maharashtra state agency.
articles.image_caption: An HDFC Bank branch in India. The country's largest private lender faces a US class action lawsuit alleging deposit scheme fraud and securities violations.
articles.nri_angle: HDFC Bank is one of the most widely held Indian stocks among NRI investors, and the class action directly affects those who purchased securities on the NYSE between July 2023 and May 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Qatar Loses $24 Billion as LNG Exports Collapse 96 Percent in Hormuz Crisis
articles.excerpt: The Gulf state has exported just 18 LNG cargoes in six months, down from 509 a year earlier, while damage to the Ras Laffan complex could take five years to repair.
articles.image_caption: Qatar's LNG industry has been devastated by the Hormuz crisis, with exports collapsing 96 percent and costing the country $24 billion in lost revenue.
articles.nri_angle: The LNG supply crisis is driving up energy costs globally, with India among the hardest-hit importers and European gas prices threatening household budgets for NRIs across the continent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Falls Over 1% After U.S. PCE Inflation Data Comes in Line With Expectations
articles.excerpt: Spot gold drops to $4,594 per ounce as the Fed's preferred inflation gauge shows 3.7% annual rise, keeping rate hike prospects alive.
articles.nri_angle: Gold remains a favored asset among Indian-American investors, and U.S. inflation and Fed policy directly affect both dollar-denominated gold prices and remittance economics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oil Drops Over $2 as Iran-Oman Talks Revive Hopes for Strait of Hormuz Reopening
articles.excerpt: Brent crude falls to a two-week low after the two countries discuss a temporary navigational corridor and mine clearance in the vital waterway.
articles.nri_angle: Lower oil prices would ease fuel and transportation costs globally, while a Hormuz reopening could stabilize energy markets that affect inflation in the US and India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bitcoin Tops $80,000 for First Time Since May as Dollar Weakens on Treasury Buyback Plans
articles.excerpt: The cryptocurrency has rallied 28% in August, its best month since November 2024, as investors pile into the debasement trade amid growing U.S. fiscal concerns.
articles.image_caption: A representation of Bitcoin. The cryptocurrency topped $80,000 for the first time since May as the U.S. dollar weakened on Treasury buyback plans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Sugar Market Swings From Surplus to Shortage as Prices Hit Record Ahead of Festivals
articles.excerpt: What began as a season of oversupply and falling prices has turned into a scramble to contain record sugar costs, forcing New Delhi to allow imports for the first time in nearly a decade.
articles.image_caption: YouTube / India Today
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sensex, Nifty Reverse Intraday Losses to Close Higher as Crude Oil Falls 3%
articles.excerpt: Indian benchmarks recovered from early-session weakness as oil dropped to a one-week low, while the first monthly Nifty derivatives expiry under the new closing auction system drove sharp late-session swings.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai. The Sensex and Nifty reversed intraday losses to close higher as crude oil prices fell sharply.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
